sections.content: If you're searching for real estate deals in Huntington WV, you've likely already noticed something that seasoned investors have quietly figured out: this mid-sized West Virginia city offers some of the most affordable entry points in the entire eastern United States. With median home prices sitting well below $150,000 and a steady demand for rental housing driven by two major universities and a regional healthcare hub, Huntington punches above its weight for investors willing to look past the surface. Whether you're a first-time buyer or an experienced wholesaler expanding your portfolio, this guide covers everything you need to know. If you're brand new to the game, start with our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in.
Huntington WV Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Huntington is the second-largest city in West Virginia, home to roughly 45,000 residents and anchored by Marshall University and the Cabell Huntington Hospital system — the area's largest employer. These two economic pillars create consistent demand for both rental housing and owner-occupied homes. The city sits at the convergence of West Virginia, Kentucky, and Ohio, giving it a regional draw that many purely rural Appalachian markets lack. Unlike some struggling small cities, Huntington has attracted ongoing federal investment, downtown revitalization funding, and infrastructure improvements over the last five years. That slow-burn recovery is exactly the kind of environment where real estate investors can find undervalued assets before prices move.
Average Home Prices and What Your Dollar Gets You

As of 2024, the median home price in Huntington WV hovers around $105,000 to $125,000, depending on the neighborhood and condition. That's roughly one-fifth of the national median, which means your capital goes dramatically further here. Single-family homes in move-in condition in desirable neighborhoods like Westmoreland and Guyandotte typically list between $130,000 and $200,000. Distressed properties — the bread and butter of wholesale and flip deals — can be acquired for as little as $20,000 to $60,000 in areas like Highlawn or Central City, with after-repair values (ARVs) often landing between $85,000 and $130,000. Before you commit to any deal, run your numbers through our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to make sure the math actually works.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Huntington
Westmoreland — Best for Buy-and-Hold Rentals

Westmoreland is one of Huntington's most stable residential neighborhoods, featuring tree-lined streets, older craftsman-style homes, and proximity to Marshall University. Rental demand here is consistent year-round, with college students and young professionals making up a large portion of the tenant base. Expect to pay $110,000 to $160,000 for a solid rental property, with monthly rents ranging from $750 to $1,100 for a two- or three-bedroom home. Cash-on-cash returns of 8% to 12% are achievable for investors who buy right.
Highlawn — Best for Fix-and-Flip Deals

Highlawn sits just west of downtown and contains a dense mix of distressed properties and motivated sellers. This is where many local wholesalers and flippers concentrate their efforts. Acquisition prices for properties needing significant work can fall between $25,000 and $55,000, while fully renovated comparable homes sell in the $90,000 to $120,000 range. The spread is real, but so is the work — many homes here need full rehabs including roof, HVAC, plumbing, and cosmetic updates. Budget conservatively and you can still clear $20,000 to $40,000 in gross profit per flip.
Guyandotte — Best for Appreciation and Retail Buyers

Guyandotte is a historic neighborhood along the Ohio River that has seen growing interest from buyers seeking character homes at affordable prices. It attracts a mix of first-time homebuyers and remote workers relocating from higher-cost metros. Investors who can renovate thoughtfully and market to retail buyers will find a receptive audience. Properties here tend to sell faster than in Highlawn, which reduces your carrying cost risk on flips.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Huntington WV

items: Wholesale Deals: Huntington has a strong pipeline of motivated sellers due to aging housing stock and a high proportion of older homeowners. Wholesalers can assign contracts for assignment fees of $5,000 to $15,000 on most deals. Read our full guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) to understand the mechanics before you start.

Fix-and-Flip: With low acquisition costs and predictable ARVs, Huntington is a forgiving market for new flippers who manage their rehab budgets carefully. The 70% rule is your best friend here — use our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to stress-test every offer before you make it.

Long-Term Rentals (Buy-and-Hold): Marshall University's 13,000-student enrollment creates year-round rental demand in neighborhoods within two miles of campus. Section 8 vouchers are also widely accepted in Huntington, providing landlords with guaranteed government-backed rent payments.

Short-Term Rentals: Huntington hosts a growing number of regional events, Marshall University sporting events, and medical travelers visiting Cabell Huntington Hospital. Airbnb and VRBO occupancy rates in well-located properties average 55% to 70%, with nightly rates between $80 and $150.

Tax Lien and Probate Deals: West Virginia has a straightforward tax lien process, and Cabell County regularly has properties available through tax sales. Probate deals are also common given the area's aging demographic — many of the best off-market deals in Huntington come from estate sales.

sections.content: Local Market Trends Shaping Huntington Real Estate in 2024 and Beyond

Several trends are worth tracking if you want to stay ahead of the market. First, remote work migration is slowly bringing buyers from Columbus, Charlotte, and Pittsburgh who are trading high housing costs for Huntington's affordability and quality of life. Second, the downtown Huntington revitalization project — supported by federal Opportunity Zone funding — is adding restaurants, retail, and renovated commercial space that improves the neighborhood desirability of adjacent residential areas. Third, West Virginia's population decline has stabilized somewhat in Cabell County, partly due to Marshall University's growth and the healthcare sector's continued expansion. None of these are explosive growth signals, but they point toward a market floor that is firming up — which is exactly what value investors want to see.
The best real estate markets for investors aren't always the hottest ones — they're the ones where the numbers work, the population is stable, and everyone else is still looking the other way.
How to Find Off-Market Deals in Huntington WV

On-market MLS listings in Huntington can offer value, but the real money is in deals that never hit Zillow. Probate filings at Cabell County Courthouse, delinquent tax lists, and direct mail to absentee landlords are three of the highest-converting lead sources in this market. Driving for dollars — literally driving through target neighborhoods and noting vacant or distressed properties — still works exceptionally well in Huntington because a large percentage of local sellers are not actively marketing their properties. For a full breakdown of how to find deals before they hit the open market, read our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals). You can also browse verified deal opportunities directly at [aiwholesail.com/markets/huntington-wv](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/huntington-wv).

Pro Tip: Build a relationship with at least one local probate attorney in Huntington. Estates in Cabell County frequently include properties that heirs want to sell quickly and without hassle. Being a cash buyer with a fast close timeline makes you the obvious solution — and you'll often pay below market with no competition.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Looking at Huntington WV

Huntington is a manageable market for remote investors, but a few ground rules will save you from costly mistakes. West Virginia has specific landlord-tenant laws that differ from other states — familiarize yourself with the West Virginia Residential Landlord-Tenant Act before you sign a lease. Property management fees in Huntington typically run 8% to 10% of collected rent, which is in line with national averages and easy to model into your cash flow analysis. Once you've got a deal in your sights, [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) will walk you through every number you need to check before you commit.

items: Build your local team first: You need a reliable general contractor, a property manager, and a real estate attorney before you close your first deal remotely.
Use virtual wholesalers and local bird dogs: Several active wholesalers in Huntington work with out-of-state buyers regularly and can source deals on your behalf for a fee.

Visit at least once before buying: A single trip to walk properties and neighborhoods will give you context that no spreadsheet can provide. Huntington is a 3-4 hour drive from Columbus, Charlotte, or Pittsburgh.

Understand flood zone designations: Parts of Huntington sit near the Ohio and Guyandotte Rivers. Always check FEMA flood maps before purchasing, as flood insurance can significantly impact your cash flow.

Start conservative on rehab estimates: Labor and material costs in West Virginia are lower than national averages, but aging housing stock often reveals hidden issues once walls are opened. Build a 15% to 20% contingency buffer into every rehab budget.
